# New renderings — iliad-102 (16.306–393)

Format as the house table: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἡγεμόνων (ἀνὴρ ἕλεν ἄνδρα … ἡγεμόνων, 16.306–307) | "a man took a man … of the leaders" | "one of the leaders killed a man" | "each leader"; line 306 without ἡγεμόνων is iliad-094’s (15.328) and its English is reused word for word inside this longer unit; ἡγεμών "leader" (kept apart from ἄρχος "commander") |
| Φυλεΐδης (16.313) | "Phyleus’-son" | "the son of Phyleus" | "Meges" (not named in the Greek; the note names him); patronymic rule of Ἀτρεΐδης, 5.72 |
| Νεστορίδαι (plural, 16.317) | "Nestor’s-sons" | "the sons of Nestor" | "Nestor’s sons"; follows the table’s Νεστορίδης (6.33) and the patronymic hyphen |
| Ὀϊλιάδης (16.330) | "Oileus’-son" | "son of Oileus" | the table’s Ὀϊλιάδην row (12.365) |
| ἀντίθεος Θρασυμήδης (16.321) | "godlike Thrasymedes" | "godlike Thrasymedes" | "heavenly" (δῖος), "god-resembling" (θεοείκελος); ἀντίθεος "godlike" as the table’s own reservations say |
| ἀρήϊος Μενέλαος (16.311) | "warlike Menelaus" | "warlike Menelaus" | table row (3.339), unchanged |
| Μενοιτίου ἄλκιμος υἱός (16.307) | "Menoetius’ sturdy son" | "Menoetius’ sturdy son" | table row (11.605), unchanged |
| ἔγχεϊ ὀξυόεντι · ὀξέϊ δουρί (16.309; 16.317) | "with his sharp spear" · "with sharp spear" | "with his sharp spear" | "pointed"; table ἔγχος ὀξυόεν (5.50) |
| Ἀρηΐλυκος · Ἄμφικλος · Ἀτύμνιος · Μάρις · Κλεόβουλος · Λύκων · Ἀκάμας · Ἐρύμας · Ἀμισώδαρος · Πηνέλεως | Areilycus · Amphiclus · Atymnius · Maris · Cleobulus · Lycon · Acamas · Erymas · Amisodarus · Peneleos | same | Latinised forms as for the other names of the poem (Peneleos is the table’s own spelling); Θόας "Thoas"; Ἔρεβος "Erebus" |
| δοκεύσας (16.313) | "having watched for" | "watched … (and)" | "ambushed", "lain in wait" (decide too much); δοκεύω "watch, lie in wait for" |
| ἐφορμηθέντα (16.313) | "as he rushed at him" | "rush at him" | "charging", "attacking"; ἐφορμάομαι "rush at" |

| πρυμνὸν σκέλος · πρυμνὸν βραχίονα (16.314, 16.323) | "the leg at its root" · "the upper arm at its root" | "the leg at its root" · "his arm, at its root" | "the base of the leg", "the thigh"; follows the table’s πρυμνήν "at the root" (5.292) |
| πάχιστος μυών (16.314–315) | "thickest the muscle" | "a man’s muscle is thickest" | "thickest muscle", "the biggest muscle"; μυών "muscle", παχύς "thick" |
| κασιγνήτοιο χολωθείς (16.320) | "angered for his brother" | "angry for his brother" | "angered by his brother’s death" (supplies the cause); χολόω keeps "anger" (χόλος) |
| αὐτοσχεδά (16.319) | "at close quarters" | "at close quarters" | table’s αὐτοσχεδόν, unchanged |
| δουρὸς ἀκωκή (16.323) | "the tip of the spear" | "the tip of the spear" | "point" (kept for αἰχμή, used at 16.315), "edge"; the table’s ἀκωκή "tip" (11.253) |
| δρύψ’ ἀπὸ μυώνων (16.324) | "tore away from the muscles" | "tore … away from the muscles" | "flayed", "stripped"; δρύπτω "tear" |
| δούπησεν (16.325) | "fell with a thud" | "fell with a thud" | "thudded" (the first draft’s `l`; the published `l` of the same words, iliad-026 and 097, is "he fell with a thud"), "crashed" (kept for ἤριπε), "groaned"; δουπέω from δοῦπος "thud" (also 16.361) |

| υἷες ἀκοντισταί (16.328) | "sons, javelin-throwers" | "javelin-throwers" | "spearmen" (kept for αἰχμητής), "javelineers"; ἀκοντιστής from ἀκοντίζω "cast" (4.490) |

| κακὸν ἀνθρώποισιν (16.329) | "an evil to many men" | "an evil to many men" | "bane", "scourge" |
| ζωὸν ἕλε (16.331) | "took him alive" | "took him alive" | "captured"; ἕλε "took" |
| βλαφθέντα κατὰ κλόνον (16.331) | "hindered in the turmoil" | "who was hindered in the turmoil" | "stumbling", "stunned", "disabled" (decide what hindered him); βλαφθέντα "hindered" (15.484), κλόνος "turmoil" (5.167) |
| λῦσε μένος (16.332) | "loosed his might" | "loosed his might" | "took his strength", "killed him"; idiom kept whole as the table’s λῦσε γυῖα; μένος "might" (5.470) |
| ξίφει κωπήεντι (16.332) | "with a hilted sword" | "with a hilted sword" | "with a hilt-fitted sword", "hilted blade"; κώπη "hilt", ξίφος "sword" |
| ὑπεθερμάνθη (16.333) | "grew warm beneath" | "grew warm" | "was heated", "grew hot", "was warmed through" (decide how much); ὑπο- left untranslated in `i`, note says so |
| τὸν δὲ κατ’ ὄσσε ἔλλαβε πορφύρεος θάνατος καὶ μοῖρα κραταιή (16.333–334) | "and him, down over the eyes, seized purple death and strong fate" | "and purple death and strong fate seized him, down over his eyes" | the published English of 5.83 (iliad-027), reused for this half-sentence |
| συνέδραμον (16.335, 16.337) | "ran together" | "closed with one another" · "closed again" | "clashed", "met", "charged each other"; συντρέχω "run together" |
| ἤμβροτον ἀλλήλων · μέλεον ἠκόντισαν (16.335–336) | "missed one another" · "idly they both cast" | "missed one another" · "both casting to no purpose" | "in vain" (the Iliad table turned it down for μέλεον "idle"), "wretchedly" (the usual sense of the adjective); the adverb is "idly" in `l` |
| ἔγχεσι · ξιφέεσσι (16.335, 16.337) | "with spears" · "with swords" | "with their spears" · "with swords" | ἔγχος "spear" (3.338), ξίφος "sword" (2.45) |
| ἱπποκόμου κόρυθος φάλον (16.338) | "the horse-plumed helmet’s ridge" | "the ridge of the helmet with its horsehair plume" | "crest" (kept for λόφος); follows the table’s ἱπποκόμος (12.339) and φάλος "ridge" (3.362, note: sense not certain) |

| φάσγανον (16.339) | "sword" | "sword" | "blade", "brand"; two words for "sword" (ξίφος, φάσγανον), one English |

| πλήθουσι ῥέοντες (16.389) | "are full, flowing" | "run full" | "swell", "overflow"; πλήθω "be full" |
| κλιτῦς … ἀποτμήγουσι χαράδραι (16.390) | "slopes … the ravines cut away" | "hillsides … the ravines cut away" | "gorges", "gullies" (kept distinct from χαράδρη "ravine", 4.454); κλιτύς "slope" |
| ἅλα πορφυρέην (16.391) | "the purple sea" | "the purple sea" | "dark", "wine-dark"; the table’s πορφύρεος "purple" |
| ἐπικάρ (16.392) | "head first" | "plunging" | "headlong" (reserved for πρηνής, προτροπάδην), "steeply", "from above" (each decides the unknown); note: formed on the root of κάρη, sense not certain |
| μινύθει … ἔργ’ ἀνθρώπων (16.392) | "the works of men grow less" | "the works of men dwindle away" | "waste", "are destroyed"; μινύθω intransitive "grow less" (transitive "lessens", 15.491) |
| Τρῳαὶ μεγάλα στενάχοντο θέουσαι (16.393) | "the Trojan mares greatly groaned, running" | "the Trojan mares groaned loudly as they ran" | "horses" (loses the feminine); στενάχω "groan" (1.364) |
